key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over days to weeks. LOCATION: BILATERAL weakness, usually starting with eyes. DURATION: Progressive over days to weeks. CHARACTER: PROGRESSIVE weakness, fatigue. AGGRAVATING: ACTIVITY, stress, fatigue. RELIEVING: CHOLINESTERASE inhibitors, immunosuppressants. TIMING: Progressive over days to weeks. SEVERITY: 4-8/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: PROGRESSIVE WEAKNESS, double vision, drooping eyelids, difficulty swallowing, breathing problems, fatigue. KEY POSITIVES: Progressive weakness, double vision, drooping eyelids, difficulty swallowing, breathing problems. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe respiratory distress - possible respiratory failure, call 911
Signs of respiratory failure - difficulty breathing, cyanosis, altered mental status - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
Signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
